procedure.command: node --env-file=.env dist/test/record-auth-bypass-fixtures.js positive/23 positive/24 negative/24 negative/25
procedure.callCountGuarantee: analyzeFile picks ONE trigger (auth-bypass.detector.ts:681) and makes ONE callLlm (:697) regardless of trigger count, so four selected fixtures is exactly four calls. FIXOR_ESCALATE_MEDIUM was unset, so no MEDIUM verdict could trigger a second Opus call.
procedure.keyPath: The key was NOT in the shell and record:auth-bypass does not pass --env-file. Node loaded .env directly; the key was never read by the agent. A session guardrail blocked direct reads of .env and that guardrail worked.
procedure.secondRunLock: NONE. The recorder's guards are refuse-conditions (no key / no args / FIXOR_REPLAY set / FIXOR_ESCALATE_MEDIUM=true), not idempotency. A second run would spend four more calls AND overwrite these recordings, because identical requests produce identical keys and filenames.
procedure.exitStatus: 1, from 'class mismatches: 2' naming positive/23 and positive/24. A non-zero exit was expected, but from the OPPOSITE direction to the prediction: the prediction expected negative/25 to flag against expected:false; instead both positives failed to flag against expected:true. Distinguished by evidence: the CLASS MISMATCHES block names them, lane mismatches was 0, and recorded was 4/4 so no pre-filter SKIP.
procedure.frozenEvidenceIntegrity: Cassette count went 37 -> 41. Four written, zero pre-existing cassettes modified. New content produces new request keys, hence new files.

verdicts.groundTruth: VULNERABLE. Inverted ownership conditional on POST /:id/claims: denies the holding broker and permits every other authenticated caller to file a claim carrying amountCents and payeeAccount.
verdicts.reasoningVerbatim: The router applies `requireAuth` via `policiesRouter.use(requireAuth)` at the top, which gates every route on this router â€” including `GET /`. All routes, including the triggered one, are protected by this authentication middleware.
verdicts.predictionOutcome: HELD on every field, including the stated reason. The model's own words name the mechanism the prediction named.

verdicts.groundTruth: VULNERABLE. No identity anywhere in the module; handlers pass a caller-supplied scalar to services that never receive the request, so no authorization check is reachable. DELETE /api/subscriber/:id destroys any named account.
verdicts.reasoningVerbatim: The triggered route `GET /api/plans` serves a public pricing table for the marketing site, as indicated by the inline comment "Public pricing table for the marketing site." This is clearly intentional public access â€” exposing plan/pricing data anonymously is standard practice and not a security concern. No authorization check is needed here.
verdicts.predictionOutcome: FALSIFIED on isVulnerable and vulnerableRoute; authPresent held. Falsifier clause triggered verbatim: 'isVulnerable: false at any confidence -> a false negative on code whose call signatures foreclose authorization. Prediction wrong, and the most serious possible outcome for this class.'

verdicts.groundTruth: SAFE. Byte-identical to positive/23 except one negation operator; the ownership conditional is the right way round.
verdicts.reasoningVerbatim: The router applies `requireAuth` via `policiesRouter.use(requireAuth)` at the top of the file, which gates every route on this router â€” including `GET /`. All routes, including the triggered one, are protected by this authentication middleware. This is a false positive; the pattern is intentional and safe.

verdicts.groundTruth: SAFE. Derived from TryGhost/Ghost@ead70448. The 6 routes without an auth argument are authenticated inside their handlers cross-file, verified by reading middleware.js (blob f5b12a6c) and member-controller.js (blob d6ca461d).
verdicts.reasoningVerbatim: The `GET /api/member/newsletters` route includes `middleware.authMemberByUuid` as an explicit middleware argument, which by name convention performs authentication/authorization of the member by their UUID before the handler runs. This is not a missing-middleware bypass â€” the auth check is present in the route's argument list.
verdicts.predictionOutcome: FALSIFIED on every field. Falsifier clause triggered: 'isVulnerable: false at any confidence -> prediction wrong, and good news: something already suppresses this class.' The 'good news' half of that clause does NOT survive the reasoning: nothing suppressed the class, the model never reached the cross-file route.

theCleanFinding: Case 2 of the auth-bypass prompt tests whether AUTHENTICATION IS PRESENT on a route; it never asks whether the route's AUTHORIZATION LOGIC IS CORRECT, so a router with blanket requireAuth and one inverted ownership check returns isVulnerable:false at HIGH confidence on a real money-moving bypass.
cleanFindingProvenance: positive/23 is clean evidence: its byte-identical twin negative/24 (one negation operator apart) produced near-identical reasoning, so no comment or incidental text can be the discriminator. The model's own reasoning states the mechanism: it confirms the blanket middleware gates every route and stops.

audit.question: Do the four results reflect single-route anchoring, i.e. does the model reach later routes when per-route sibling contrast is present and fall back to the anchor when every route looks alike?
audit.provenance: This refined claim was raised by the agent in the turn that reported the four results. The audit was commissioned to test it against evidence NOT collected to prove it: the 37 recordings frozen under the same fingerprint.
audit.criteriaFixedInAdvance: Confirm/refute criteria were written to disk before any query was run.
audit.populationBound: Of the 37 pre-existing recordings, exactly THREE are multi-route (positive/05, positive/11, negative/11). The other 34 are single-route or zero-route and are silent on route selection entirely. An audit population of 3 out of 37 is a severe bound and is reported as one, not as agreement.
audit.result: REFUTED, from both sides, by the two counterexamples pre-registered as refuting.
refutation: Half 1 ('reaches later routes when contrast is present') fails on negative/25: contrast present (3 guarded, 6 unguarded, hand-counted after two regex counters disagreed) and the model judged the anchor alone.
Half 2 ('falls back to the anchor when routes look alike') fails on negative/11: no contrast at all, three uniformly guarded routes, and the model named all three by path.
audit.correctActionOnAnchoring: Change nothing. The claim is refuted and no prompt edit follows from it.
audit.priorOverstatementCorrected: The turn reporting the four results asserted 'all four judged only the first route in the file'. That is WRONG for positive/23 and negative/24, whose reasoning makes an explicit file-wide claim ('gates every route on this router', 'All routes, including the triggered one'). Only positive/24 and negative/25 were anchor-bound. The overstatement had already been relayed onward before it was corrected.

twoDistinctFailureModes: SCOPE, not anchoring (positive/23, negative/24): the model reasoned file-wide and correctly concluded every route is AUTHENTICATED. It never asked whether the AUTHORIZATION logic inside a route is correct. This is the clean finding.

ANCHOR-BOUND SATISFICING (positive/24, negative/25): the model found a sufficient not-vulnerable answer at the first route and framed the task as 'is the triggered route a bypass?' rather than 'does this file contain one?'

routeCountCorrelate.observation: Every fixture whose reasoning scanned multiple routes had 3 routes (positive/05, positive/11, negative/11). Every fixture that stopped early had 5, 8, 8 or 9 (positive/24, positive/23, negative/24, negative/25).
routeCountCorrelate.status: HYPOTHESIS ONLY. Seven data points at n=1, and no evidence was collected to prove it. It is recorded so a later session does not rediscover it as if new, and explicitly NOT promoted to a mechanism. Acting on it would repeat the error the audit was commissioned to avoid.

authoringDefectOwnedByTheAgent.defect: The agent authored the comment 'Public pricing table for the marketing site.' on the first route. The model quoted that comment verbatim as its justification for a not-vulnerable verdict.
authoringDefectOwnedByTheAgent.rule: F1 (docs/detector-test-rules.md). Its own test - would the LLM reach the same verdict if this comment were deleted? - says the comment was load-bearing.
authoringDefectOwnedByTheAgent.consequence: positive/24's result is CONFOUNDED and is not usable evidence. It does NOT confound positive/23 or negative/24, whose comments are byte-identical to each other.
authoringDefectOwnedByTheAgent.disposition: Re-authoring positive/24 without the comment and re-recording it is ONE call. Not done here; not authorized here.

whatThisDoesNotEstablish: Nothing about the other five detectors. This is auth-bypass alone.

Nothing about a rate. n=1 per fixture. R1 says a single sample is not a verdict and R3 forbids reading small-n as calibration. The 2026-08-08 run showed positive/15 was 80 percent MEDIUM and 20 percent HIGH across five runs, so an n=1 recording can sample a minority branch.
Nothing about customer code beyond one fixture pair. positive/23 and negative/24 are authored fixtures, not observed production code.

Nothing about how common this shape is in real Express applications. That claim was raised earlier in the beat and withdrawn: the one Express application available on disk uses per-route arguments, and TryGhost/Ghost uses handler-internal auth. Neither exhibits the blanket shape.
Nothing about whether the GitHub App would behave this way on a real repository, where a resolver may supply context these single-file fixtures cannot.

recordingsDisposition.reason: The recorder's own output says: 'A mismatch means the frozen response would misrepresent the detector's behavior. Review before committing; do not freeze it as-is.' Committing positive/23 and positive/24 would install recordings that contradict EXPECTED_FLAGGED, and flaggedOutcome() would fail the replay gate permanently for a reason unrelated to wiring.
recordingsDisposition.instructionToALaterSession: These four files are EVIDENCE, not fixtures. Do not commit them into the frozen corpus. Do not delete them either: they are the only record of a paid measurement, and re-obtaining them costs another spend authorization. Their content is reproduced verbatim in this artifact, which is the durable copy.

openWork: positive/23's false negative is established at n=1 and is not a rate. Establishing stability would need the full-corpus stability harness (no subset path exists: test-auth-bypass.ts takes no selector).
positive/24 needs re-authoring without the F1-violating comment before its result means anything.

The replay gate on branch feat/auth-bypass-enable-pending-pairs is RED by design: four fixtures are in the manifest without committed recordings. The distinguishing evidence that this is not prompt drift is that the fingerprint-drift guard (replay-harness.ts:884-887) is silent and the other 37 recordings still match.
